subject: Clarify: pro-rata audit window & evidence timestamp expectations
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@veritas-audit.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acme.com
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on partial-month coverage and timestamped evidence

Hi Stephanie,

We're finalizing the Type II packet for Acme and want to confirm one edge case around your audit period. The report lists coverage 2026-08-01 through 2027-07-31, but Acme's pre-prod migration had a cutover on 2026-12-15. A few follow-up questions: 

- For monthly inclusivity, do you consider a month "covered" if the control was in place for only part of that calendar month (e.g., from 12/15 onward)?
- When auditors request point-in-time evidence (e.g., access-control snapshots, config exports), are you able to provide items with timestamp granularity (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS), or only daily exports?
- If we need a bridge letter that confirms the pre/post cutover coverage semantics, do you have an editable draft we can attach to the packet?

If it's easier, a short confirmation email and any relevant attachment would suffice. We aim to get the final packet to the reviewer by EOD Thursday.

Thanks,
Liam
Senior Auditor | Veritas Audit Partners
liam.oconnor@veritas-audit.com

--
Attachment: sample-request-list.csv (CSV listing typical evidence docs)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@veritas-audit.com>
Cc: security@acme.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on partial-month coverage and timestamped evidence

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by details.

- Month inclusivity: We mark a calendar month as "in-scope" for SOC 2 reporting if the control was in production for any part of that month, but we annotate mid-month changes in the evidence manifest so auditors can see the exact cutover date.
- Evidence timestamping: We can provide exports with timestamp granularity (to the second) for the following artifacts: access logs (S3-hosted consolidated logs), IAM policy snapshots, and deployment manifests. For some legacy telemetry (agent heartbeats) we only have daily roll-ups — we'll flag those.
- Bridge letter: We have a templated bridge-letter draft we use for mid-period migrations; I can attach a version and a one-paragraph explanation specific to Acme's 2026-12-15 cutover.

Details / follow-ups: 
- Evidence scope: For the months that contain the cutover (2026-12), we'll provide both a pre-cutover snapshot (2026-12-14 23:59:59) and a post-cutover snapshot (2026-12-15 00:00:00+) where available. For logs, you'll get log slices that span the transition with explicit start/end timestamps.
- Sample rate: For event logs we can supply the full raw log for the 48-hour window around cutover; for longer-term evidence we typically give 7-day samples per month unless you request continuous exports.
- Labeling: All artifacts in the Drive link will include a manifest row with artifact_type, start_ts, end_ts, and a short description for auditor consumption.

I'm copying Karthik (Audit Ops) to ensure the attachments and manifest match what you need. If you want the bridge letter tailored differently, let me know the exact reviewer text and we'll adapt.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

--
Attachments: SOC2-TypeII-2026.pdf (final report), bridge-letter-draft.docx (editable draft)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@veritas-audit.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acme.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on partial-month coverage and timestamped evidence

Liam — quick operational notes so you know what to expect in the Drive package: 

- File naming: YYYYMMDD_artifactType_source.ext (e.g., 20261215_access-log-s3.jsonl)
- Timestamps: all log artifacts are in ISO 8601 with UTC offsets and to-second precision.
- Snapshot strategy: where we have database dumps or config manifests, we will include a "snapshot_metadata.txt" with precise generation timestamp and the job id that created it.
- Legacy telemetry: as Stephanie noted, agent heartbeats before 2026-11-01 were aggregated daily. We will include a short sampling note so you can understand gaps.

If you want the 48-hour full-raw logs for the cutover window packaged as a single archive, reply and we'll stage it to the Drive link; otherwise we'll include the default slices.

Thanks — Karthik
Manager, Audit Operations | Redwood Inference

--
Bcc: internal-archives@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@veritas-audit.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, security@acme.com
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on partial-month coverage and timestamped evidence

Hi Liam — attached is a bridge-letter draft tailored for Acme's 2026-12-15 migration. I made two small edits: clarified that month-of-December is reported as in-scope with annotated cutover timestamps, and added a sentence about the 48-hour raw log bundle availability on request.

Please review the paragraph starting "Scope clarification:" and let me know if the language matches what your reviewer needs. Once you sign off I'll convert to PDF and add a signature block.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Security & Compliance Program Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

--
Attachments: bridge-letter-draft.docx (editable), SOC2-TypeII-2026.pdf (referenced)
